gold-size.title: Gold nanoparticles · 16–108 nm
gold-size.description: Ten monodisperse gold sphere sizes in water, all at 2.6 ppm particle volume fraction (about 50 µg/mL Au). The inner vial diameter is 10 mm. This is an illustrative common-concentration series, not a fit to a photographed experiment.

gold-shells.title: Au shells on 120 nm silica cores
gold-shells.description: Ten monodisperse core–shell dispersions in water share 120 nm diameter silica cores. Gold shell thicknesses run from 5 to 50 nm. All samples have 10 ppm total outer-particle volume fraction, so the Au mass concentration varies with thickness. Side illumination shows the balance between transmitted and scattered colour.

bleyer-main.title: Bleyer et al. · Figs. 3 & 4 · S1300 LED concentration estimates
bleyer-main.description: Seven systems from Bleyer et al. (2025), Predictive design of plasmonic color. Core diameters and shell thicknesses are from Fig. 3 and Fig. 4. Reported mean/SD values are represented by independent lognormal number distributions, an app modeling assumption. For the broad Ag sample, the paper’s 20 nm radius (40 nm diameter) monodisperse simulation reference is used because its experimental radius range (3–24 nm) does not define a unique distribution. Concentrations are independently optimized for the paper’s target Lab colours using this app’s S1300 LED illumination, 10-degree observer, CIE76 and 1 cm direct transmission. They are not measured concentrations from the paper and the renders use the S1300 literature lamp model chosen by the authors and do not claim to recreate their raw measured lamp spectrum or camera response. Core/shell labels give core DIAMETER / shell THICKNESS in nm.

tiny-wonders.title: Ten tiny wonders · a colloid lightbox tour
tiny-wonders.description: Ten illustrative model dispersions in water, curated to demonstrate size, composition, coatings, population breadth and scattering. Concentrations differ intentionally; A/B and I/J are equal-volume-fraction pairs. These are simulations, not measured photographs. Labels use d for diameter and t for radial shell thickness. F lists arithmetic mean dimensions; its lognormal core-size and shell-thickness CVs are 15% and 30%.

presentationNotes.title: Ruby gold
presentationNotes.whatToTry: Small gold: coloured transmission with a comparatively clear dispersion. Try the transparency card.

presentationNotes.title: Gold grows up
presentationNotes.whatToTry: Same particle volume fraction as A, larger spheres: compare transmission, scattering and angular lobes.

presentationNotes.title: Silver sunshine
presentationNotes.whatToTry: 20 nm Ag at 24 ppm by volume: stronger golden transmission. Compare back and front illumination and contrast with the gold sphere.

presentationNotes.title: Silver changes character
presentationNotes.whatToTry: Larger silver changes the resonance and scattering/transmission balance.

presentationNotes.title: A gold skin on glass
presentationNotes.whatToTry: A 120 nm silica core with a 15 nm gold shell: compare opposite lighting directions and side-lit edges.

presentationNotes.title: Same mean, broader population
presentationNotes.whatToTry: Same mean dimensions and total volume fraction as E; independent lognormal core and shell distributions (15% and 30% CV).

presentationNotes.title: Silver core, gold skin
presentationNotes.whatToTry: An 80 nm silver core with a 5 nm gold shell: optical behaviour comes from both metals and their interfaces.

presentationNotes.title: Silicon joins the show
presentationNotes.whatToTry: A 160 nm crystalline-silicon sphere. Open in lesson 05 to inspect the dielectric multipoles and angular pattern.

presentationNotes.title: Almost clear latex
presentationNotes.whatToTry: 80 nm PS at the same volume fraction as J. Compare how clear it remains and inspect side scattering.

presentationNotes.title: Milk and a warm shadow
presentationNotes.whatToTry: 300 nm PS: front illumination is milky; back illumination and a pale side-lit support reveal a warmer transmitted component.

traore-alloys.title: Traoré 2023 · Fig. 3 · Ag–Au alloy series
traore-alloys.description: Ten compositions from Fig. 3, omitting xAu = 0.8. Rioux alloy optical functions with the paper’s composition-dependent finite-size Drude correction: CAg=0.2959, CAu=0.2035, linearly interpolated; app A=4C/3 under L=4V/S. The pure Ag/Au endpoints use the paper’s Fig. 1 mean diameters and SDs (4.47±0.56 and 5.1±0.67 nm); intermediate alloy sizes remain representative 6.5 nm because individual Fig. 3 distributions are not tabulated. Recipe: 1 μmol total metal in 6 mL, full conversion assumed. Water medium and 10 mm path; dextran shell omitted. The photograph’s lighting and vial path are not calibrated to this scene.

evanoff-best.title: Evanoff & Chumanov 2004 · Ten best Ag fits
evanoff-best.description: The ten lowest-residual panel fits (E–N) from Figure 2, ordered by fitted mean diameter. Each panel uses its best match across the four available silver datasets and both constrained one-parameter fit modes. The chosen dataset and fit mode are retained for each sample. All use A = 1, the original lognormal number distribution and Hale–Querry water. Labels give calculation mean diameter and SD, not necessarily the reported TEM values. At the SD bound, the fit remains a bounded optical estimate. All samples have the same illustrative loading, 20 mg Ag/L, in 10 mm cuvettes under D65; the absolute per-particle figure does not determine the experimental loading.

source.selection: Best of four optical datasets × two one-parameter modes per panel, then ten lowest panel residuals; ascending calculation mean diameter.

oldenburg-best.title: Oldenburg 1998 · Gold nanoshell growth · Best fits
oldenburg-best.description: Eight nanoshell interpretations from Figures 3a and 3b. Four small-core and four large-core samples retain the fitted lognormal distributions, one shared core population per family, Olmon/McPeak Au and A = 1 with L = 4V/S. The rising 3b trace is interpreted as a thin complete shell with a constant vertical plotting offset. Only its particle model is rendered. All samples use an illustrative 20 mg Au/L, not a concentration inferred from the historical plot. Labels give mean core diameter and mean shell thickness ± shell SD in nm. Core and shell sizes are optical fits rather than independent structural measurements.

lycurgus-seidel.title: Lycurgus effect · alloy and glass analogues

scientificBasis.purpose: Illustrate red transmission and olive-green reflection in the supplied mug. These are optical analogues, not a recovered archaeological recipe.
scientificBasis.closestExistingMaterial: Rioux Au–Ag alloy at x_Au = 0.30, a binary approximation to the reported Ag–Au–Cu particles.
scientificBasis.appearanceVariants: The two x_Au = 0.20 samples deliberately favour the optical colour contrast. They are not presented as the measured composition of the cup.
scientificBasis.matrix: Measured modern soda–lime clear glass, Rubin 1985. The alternative green glass can be selected in Scene settings. Neither is measured Lycurgus glass.
scientificBasis.silica: The x_Au = 0.30 example includes 0.3 vol% 200 nm silica spheres as a simple proxy for silica-rich scattering regions. The real glass is more heterogeneous.
scientificBasis.rendering: Same particle and matrix parameters in front and back lighting. A = 1 for every size-distribution member. Narrow photographic front illumination, D65.
